distribution.title:
The primary purpose of collecting and generating data for this project is to develop, validate, and implement a peatland revitalization hydrological model that integrates hydrological, ecological, and socio-economic factors to optimize peatland restoration strategies. This model will support the sustainable management of peatlands and mires in alignment with the EU Green Deal objectives, particularly focusing on climate change mitigation, biodiversity conservation, and water resource management. Hydrological data collection is essential for capturing groundwater level fluctuations, surface water dynamics, and overall mire and peatland hydrology. These data will support the calibration and validation of the METQ conceptual hydrological model, ensuring its applicability to peatland ecosystems. The model will simulate water movement, storage, and exchange between peatlands, groundwater, and surface water systems, which is critical for evaluating different restoration interventions, such as rewetting, controlled flooding, and drainage blocking.
Meteorological data, including daily and hourly records of precipitation and temperature will be used to quantify climatic influences on peatland hydrology. These datasets are fundamental for accurately modeling water balance, hydrological fluxes, and ecosystem responses to climatic variability. Groundwater and surface water monitoring data will be sourced from the Latvia University of Life Sciences and Technology, Forest and Water Resources Laboratory, which has maintained long-term groundwater level and water temperature records from both degraded and natural peatlands. These records will provide a critical baseline for assessing the impacts of past and future restoration efforts. The collected datasets will support scenario-based simulations to assess various restoration strategies under different climate and land-use scenarios. The model will serve as a decision-support tool, helping to optimize peatland restoration efforts by maximizing water retention, carbon sequestration, and biodiversity conservation.

dataset.title: Climate and groundwater level data

dmp.description:
Wetland ecosystems, including mires, play a crucial role in biodiversity conservation, water purification, carbon sequestration, and climate regulation. However, many mires have been degraded due to anthropogenic activities such as drainage, peat extraction, and land-use changes, leading to the loss of their ecological functions. The restoration of peatland hydrological regimes has become a priority in environmental management and policy, particularly within the framework of the EU Green Deal, which aims to achieve climate neutrality and restore biodiversity by 2050.
This project focuses on developing and validating a wetland revitalization hydrological model that integrates hydrological, ecological, and socio-economic factors to optimize restoration strategies. The model will build upon the METQ conceptual hydrological model, extending its applicability to wetland hydrology and incorporating ecological and land management components.
The key datasets for model development and validation include meteorological data (daily and hourly records of precipitation and temperature), hydrological and hydrogeological data (groundwater level and surface water dynamics measured at both degraded and natural peatlands). The collected datasets will support model calibration, validation, and scenario-based simulations to assess different wetland restoration strategies. The model's predictive capability will allow for evaluating the effectiveness of rewetting, controlled flooding, and other hydrological interventions under various climate and land-use scenarios.
The collected datasets will support model calibration, validation, and scenario-based simulations to predict the outcomes of restoration interventions under different climate and land-use scenarios. The integration of real-time monitoring data will facilitate adaptive peatland management, early warning systems for hydrological stress, and sustainable water resource planning.
